country.evidence_quote: Professor Serge P. Hoogendoorn is an expert in the field of traffic and transportation engineering. He is a distinguished professor in Smart Urban at Delft University of Technology in the Netherlands. With a strong focus on traffic flow theory, pedestrian and crowd dynamics, and intelligent transportation systems, Professor Hoogendoorn has significantly contributed to advancing knowledge in traffic and transportation domain. external_collaboration.evidence_quote: The hackathon is aimed at MSc students, PhD candidates and postdoctoral researchers at TU Delft, as well as students from Rotterdam University of Applied Sciences. Participants from different academic backgrounds are welcome! However, keep in mind that challenges will be focused on the Mobility domain.

Participants can expect real-world challenges from public and private organizations across the mobility sector, including Rijkswaterstaat, NDW, the Municipality of Rotterdam, FlixBus, and other partners. The topics span a wide range of mobility domains, such as traffic management (combining floating-car and loop-detector data to detect queue tails); climate resilience (assessing how disruptions affect traffic flow); and transport service planning (exploring pricing or supply decisions).
